context: A uni student interviews a retired emergency manager
purpose: Teach: 分裂/火災/津波/飛躍/流動/機動/抑圧/繁栄

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 先生、現役時代、津波対策の現場、どうでしたか。
lines.en: Sensei, what was the tsunami-response field like when you were active?
lines.style: Respectful inquiry, leaning forward slightly. Genuine curiosity without presumption. Careful pacing — not rushing into the next question. Warm deference in the vocal posture.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 地域によっては政策が分裂していて、調整が大変だった。
lines.en: In some regions the policy was fragmented, so the coordination was difficult.
lines.style: Measured, reflective tone. Speaking from lived experience — no performance. Slight pause before answering, as if reaching back into memory. Steady, unhurried delivery.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 火災の連動も、想定外でしたか。
lines.en: Was the cascading fire scenario something you didn't anticipate either?
lines.style: Softer follow-up, building on the previous answer. Genuine probe, not skeptical. Respectful silence underneath — inviting him to go deeper without pressure.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 機動的な対応がうまくいった地域は、住民への抑圧的指示を避けていたよ。
lines.en: In places where rapid response succeeded, they tended to avoid heavy-handed orders to residents.
lines.style: Quiet authority in this observation. Not lecturing — offering a pattern he noticed. Slight weight on the word choice, like these lessons cost something to learn. Thoughtful trailing off.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 技術の飛躍で、変わったところはありますか。
lines.en: Have technological breakthroughs changed much in that work?
lines.style: Earnest question, opening with genuine interest. Third-hour conversation energy — comfortable enough to ask something that builds. Even pace, receptive silence at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 流動的な人口データの可視化、革命的だったね。地域の繁栄にも貢献している。
lines.en: Visualizing fluid population data was revolutionary. It's contributed to local prosperity as well.
lines.style: Animated by the memory — this one genuinely struck him. Warmer, more engaged delivery. The word 'revolutionary' carries conviction. Slight lean into the second sentence, as if connecting dots aloud.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 貴重なお話、ありがとうございます。
lines.en: Thank you for sharing something so valuable.
lines.style: Sincere and quiet. Not effusive — genuine gratitude. Slight bow in the voice. Closing with warmth, not performance. Breath of finality, but gentle.
